Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Does a sensitivity slope prove the true CTE?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It describes the model's local response around the assumed input.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A controlled sensitivity run changes one declared parameter while retaining geometry, stage, loads, boundaries, and output definition. Trace the visual in order: baseline; one parameter; difference. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic exercise: vary EMC CTE by ±10% around a stated baseline and record warpage at the same process stage. Boundary: The ±10% perturbation is a synthetic classroom choice.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing
R8: IEEE TCPMT, Simulation and Experimental Study of Fan-Out Warpage | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8590768

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Synthetic exercise: vary EMC CTE by ±10% around a stated baseline and record warpage at the same process stage. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. The ±10% perturbation is a synthetic classroom choice.
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.

Connect this mechanism to the worked example: If ranking flips over the measured conductivity range, withhold the recommendation until that property or a package response is measured.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
